text: A program uses two int variables. How many distinct states can it be in?
choices: It depends on the values assigned
About 1.8 x 10^19, because the possibilities multiply
explanation: Each int has 2^32 possibilities and they are independent, so 2^32 x 2^32 = 2^64. This is why programs cannot be tested exhaustively — testing samples the space rather than covering it — and why loop invariants matter.
